topics.title: Length and Area Properties of Two-Dimensional Geometrical Figures
topics.subject: mathematics
outcomes: Describe the length of two dimensional geometrical figures. (u)
Develop, understand and state Pythagoras' theorem. (k, u)
Apply Pythagoras' theorem to right angled and isosceles triangles. (u, s)
Understands the meaning of area in two dimensional geometrical figures (triangles, rectangles). (u, s)

body.text: Pythagoras' theorem applies to any right-angled triangle: the square of the hypotenuse (the longest side, opposite the right angle) equals the sum of the squares of the other two sides.
A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 6 cm and 8 cm. The hypotenuse c satisfies c^2 = 6^2 + 8^2 = 36 + 64 = 100, so c = √100 = 10 cm.

The area of a rectangle is length x width. The area of a triangle is half the base times the perpendicular height (not the slant side), because any triangle is exactly half of the rectangle that surrounds it. A triangle with base 12 cm and perpendicular height 5 cm has area = 0.5 x 12 x 5 = 30 cm^2.

body.expr: area of triangle = 0.5 x base x height = 0.5 x 12 x 5 = 30 cm^2
